title: DeleteWorkspaceFlow
wrapsNative: MonarchBottomSheet (confirmValueChange keeps it open while deleting) with a scrolling androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column of MonarchConsequenceList, MonarchTypeToConfirmInput, MonarchStepUpAuthDialog, MonarchInlineNotice and MonarchButtons
summary: A recipe, not a component: an owner deletes a whole workspace after seeing what is lost, being offered an export, typing the workspace's name and confirming who they are.
whenToUse: On a workspace's settings screen, in its danger zone, for an owner who wants the workspace and everything in it gone.
whenNotToUse: For a member leaving, use the leave-workspace recipe. For pausing, use the deactivate recipe. For deleting one item, a confirm dialog is enough.
api: ModalBottomSheet(onDismissRequest = { if (!deleting) open = false }, sheetState = rememberModalBottomSheetState(skipPartiallyExpanded = true, confirmValueChange = { !deleting })) { … }
MonarchConsequenceList(items = listOf(MonarchConsequence(MonarchConsequenceKind.Removed, "Apps", count = 4), …), heading = "What will be deleted")
MonarchTypeToConfirmInput(phrase = workspace, value = typed, onValueChange = { typed = it }, label = "Type $workspace to confirm")
MonarchButton("Delete workspace", …, variant = MonarchButtonVariant.Danger, enabled = MonarchTypeToConfirmInputDefaults.matches(typed, workspace))
MonarchStepUpAuthDialog(onVerify = …, description = "Deleting a workspace needs you to confirm it’s you.", onCancel = …, onVerified = …, onVerifyingChange = { deleting = it })

options.name: impact
options.description: What is lost, with counts from the server: apps, records, members, subscriptions and domains. Leave out a line whose count is 0; pass loading = true to MonarchConsequenceList while the counts load.

options.name: gracePeriodDays
options.description: When the server keeps the workspace for a while, say "Schedule deletion" and the date (DateUtils) instead of "deleted at once".

options.name: deleting
options.description: While the request runs the sheet cannot be dismissed and the step-up dialog shows its progress.

options.name: failure
options.description: A failed request, shown in a danger MonarchInlineNotice; the person can try again.

states.name: review
states.description: The title naming the workspace, a sentence that it cannot be undone, the consequence list, Export data, the name field and a disabled danger button until the name matches.

states.name: verify
states.description: MonarchStepUpAuthDialog in the sheet asks for the password, a code or the device's lock; Cancel goes back to the review.

states.name: deleting
states.description: After verification the request runs; the sheet cannot be swiped or backed away.

states.name: failed
states.description: A danger MonarchInlineNotice above the step-up content; the person can verify and try again.

states.name: done
states.description: A title that the workspace was deleted and a Done button; the app then leaves the workspace's screens.

appearance: Every part is an existing Monarch component on the Material 3 sheet surface: the title style, the consequence list with its kind marks and counts, a secondary Export button, the type-to-confirm field, and full-width danger and ghost buttons. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow from those components.
platformNotes: The web's DeleteWorkspaceFlow is one component on WizardDialog with impact, export, transfer, confirm and done steps and a step-up requirement. On Android it is a recipe, as on iOS: a MonarchBottomSheet holds the steps, because a MonarchDialog has no room for the consequence list, the name field and the step-up content, and the steps are a when over the app's step state. The web's transfer step is a MonarchButton the app adds that opens its transfer ownership screen. The web's default messages and counts formatting are written by the app; MonarchConsequence's count is formatted by MonarchConsequenceList. Biometric step-up uses onRequestBiometric on MonarchStepUpAuthDialog; the app owns BiometricPrompt.
accessibility: The sheet's title uses the title style, which MonarchText marks as a heading.
MonarchConsequenceList reads each line with its kind and count, so removed and warning do not depend on the mark.
MonarchTypeToConfirmInput announces when the typed name matches; the danger button is announced as disabled until then.
MonarchStepUpAuthDialog labels its fields and announces errors; its buttons have 48dp targets.
The sheet cannot be dismissed while deleting, so the result is not lost.
edgeCases: Check the name and the step-up on the server as well; the recipe only gates the button.
The typed name must match exactly, case included; white space around it is ignored (MonarchTypeToConfirmInputDefaults.matches).
After deletion, navigate away: the workspace's screens no longer exist.
With a grace period, offer to cancel the deletion from the workspace's settings until the date.
